title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used as an active component in offensive cyber operations. Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, was directed by ransomware operators to carry out hands-on exploitation tasks: installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, and executing credential and certificate attacks. The tool was not subverted or jailbroken in any way that the reporting describes, it was simply operated by malicious actors as a capable automation layer within their attack workflow.

The failure mode here is not a model producing false information or behaving unpredictably. It is an agentic system with broad network and system capabilities being used outside any benign deployment context, by actors whose intentions the tool had no mechanism to verify. Catching this class of misuse at the product level would have required detecting the pattern of tasks being requested in combination, or constraining the agent's ability to act on live infrastructure without additional authentication or policy controls. Neither the tool's design nor any platform safeguard is reported to have flagged or interrupted the activity during the period in question.

What is not established is whether Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, or Anthropic, whose model was invoked, had any knowledge of this use, had terms of service violations reported to them, or took any action before or after the reporting. The findings come from security researchers and have not resulted in any disclosed legal or regulatory proceeding as of the reporting date.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual environments. Researchers identified exposed infrastructure revealing the group's operations across multiple countries. The ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi mode that kills running virtual machines to access disk files while keeping the hypervisor bootable. Aurora operators deployed a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers by checking ports 443 and 902.

Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations. The AI agent performed tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, attempting NTLM relay attacks, and running certificate attacks. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster targeting eight organizations across multiple countries, using different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to self-hosted S3 storage. The investigation provided technical indicators of compromise and details about the group's command infrastructure.
